item.title: Scorpion peppers caused him ‘crippling’ pain. Two years later, The ER bill stung him again.
item.description: Maxwell Kruzic said he was in such "crippling" stomach pain on Oct. 5, 2023, that he had to pull off the road twice as he drove himself to the emergency room at Mercy Regional Medical Center in Durango, Colorado. "It was the worst pain of my life," he said.

item.title: States advance medical debt protections as federal support turns to opposition
item.description: Lawmakers in several states are working to expand medical debt protections for patients, even after the Trump administration reversed course and told states they don't have authority to take action on credit reporting.

item.title: Genes and biological networks that drive long COVID risk
item.description: This study merges causal genetics and network theory, revealing 32 genes linked to long COVID, offering insights for diagnostics and personalized therapies.

item.title: Guns marketed for personal safety fuel public health crisis in Black communities
item.description: Leon Harris, 35, is intimately familiar with the devastation guns can inflict. Robbers shot him in the back nearly two decades ago, leaving him paralyzed from the chest down. The bullet remains lodged in his spine.

item.title: World Health Organization validates Brazil's elimination of mother-to-child HIV transmission
item.description: The World Health Organization (WHO) has validated Brazil for the elimination of mother-to-child transmission (EMTCT) of HIV, making it the most populous country in the Americas to achieve this historic milestone.

item.title: Blocking platelet-activating factor reduces liver damage in cirrhosis
item.description: Researchers from Miguel Hernández University of Elche (UMH) in Spain have identified an effective strategy to reduce structural liver damage and improve hepatic vascular function in cirrhosis.

item.title: First Europe-wide analysis reveals widespread raccoon roundworm infection
item.description: The raccoon roundworm Baylisascaris procyonis can cause severe diseases in humans, including fatal brain damage.

item.title: Plastic waste transformed into building blocks for cancer drugs
item.description: A groundbreaking discovery led by the University of St Andrews has found a way to turn ordinary household plastic waste into the building block for anti-cancer drugs.

item.title: Oral health gains global recognition in WHO NCD declaration
item.description: The European Federation of Periodontology (EFP) welcomes the adoption of the WHO political declaration on noncommunicable diseases (NCDs) and mental health at the Eightieth United Nations General Assembly, recognizing it as a major step forward for integrated, people-centred health systems.

item.title: Cutting carbs, not fat, may better control appetite in women
item.description: Research indicates low-carb diets may enhance appetite regulation and reduce food cues in women with lipedema, offering a dietary intervention advantage.
